Two repairs to voice typing's Esc, both from the same report: a stray Esc ended a long dictation, and five seconds later there was no way back to it.

**You get longer to undo a long dictation** (#640)

- The Undo on a cancelled dictation used to stay for a flat five seconds. It now lasts half as long as you spoke — 20 seconds after talking for 40, up to 30 seconds — while a short dictation keeps the same five.
- A cancelled dictation is in the dictation history either way, marked 已取消 · 只存在這裡, so the text is still there to copy even after the pill has gone.

**A long dictation stops taking Esc from the app you are in** (#640)

- While Esc can cancel a dictation, Parley holds it: no other app sees it. That now ends a minute into a dictation — Esc goes back to whatever you are working in, and the dictation keeps recording.
- Cancelling a long one still works: hold your push-to-talk key and press Esc. If your trigger is fn, a plain key such as F13, or the Windows tray, where there is no such combination, Esc alone keeps cancelling as before.
